turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa). Design
variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**1. Process route dominates.** The dataset clearly contains three groups:
- Normalized-only samples (THT=30, TT=30): targets ~225–275 MPa.
- Through-hardened/quench-tempered samples (THT≈825–865, TT=420–680): targets ~325–900 MPa (higher with lower tempering TT and Si-rich spring steels).
- **Carburized samples** (NT=930, THT=30/THt=0/THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=90–540, DT=850–896, Dt=15–70, QmT=60–140, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5): targets ~838–**1190 MPa** — all the top values.

So the winning route is carburizing: CT=930, long carburizing time, diffusion at 850, low-temperature tempering (160 °C).

**2. Within the carburized group:**
- The two best samples (1124, 1190 MPa) share chemistry C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Mo=0.18, Cu=0.11, RedRatio=860. Longer carburizing (Ct=540 vs 469.8) and DT=850/Dt=15 gave 1190 vs 1124.
- Ni-Cr-Mo case-hardening chemistry (Ni≈1.6–1.7, Cr≈0.45–0.6, Mo≈0.16–0.21) consistently outperforms plain-Cr variants (e.g., Ni=0.06/Cr=1.17 group tops out ~1144).
- Low P/S and low inclusion indices (dA, dB, dC) correlate with higher strength across the dataset, so I push inclusions toward the lowest values observed in the carburized group.

**3. Proposal:** Reproduce the best-performing carburized recipe (1190 MPa row), keeping the maximum carburizing time (Ct=540), diffusion 850 °C/15 min, aggressive quench (QmT=140), tempering 160 °C/120 min, Ni-Cr-Mo chemistry, and reduce inclusion levels to the cleanest values seen in that group.

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=540, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.008, dB=0.0, dC=0.0
